clue.text: Go over only to set to rights again

parts.note: to go over a text is to read it
only, as in 'only just', means just

explanation.surface: Advice to check something solely so as to fix it once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To readjust is to correct or put back into proper order a second time.

clue.text: Inattentive serving men don't make a hit

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers serving in the British Army
to miss is to fail to hit

explanation.surface: Careless waiters failing to strike their target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving men' suggests waiters, but means soldiers: RE is the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent or careless in one's duty.

clue.text: The way of a sailor in a foreign country?

indicators.note: of here means belonging to, so the way comes after the sailor

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
a road is a way

explanation.surface: Asking about how seafarers travel when overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means overseas, away from one's home country.

clue.text: A fruity expression!

parts.note: expression is read as something pressed or squeezed out, here from fruit, not a phrase or turn of speech

explanation.definitionFit: Juice is the liquid extracted by pressing fruit.

clue.text: They ensure a good balance in the main

definitions.text: They ensure a good balance in the main

parts.words: They ensure a good balance in the main
parts.note: in the main reads as mostly, but the main is an old word for the sea, where steady footing on a rolling deck is needed

explanation.definitionFit: Sea legs are the ability to keep one's balance and avoid seasickness on board ship.

clue.text: Bores a medico with complaints

parts.note: a medico is a doctor, abbreviated DR
complaints are ailments, ills

explanation.surface: A doctor droning on about his patients' ailments is tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bores' reads as a noun for tedious people, but it is a verb: makes holes.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore a hole is to drill through material with a rotating tool.

clue.text: Air-war net being used-down it comes

indicators.note: the letters given are being used to make something else, a reworking of their order

explanation.surface: Netting deployed in an aerial battle, bringing something down.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainwater is water that falls from the sky as rain.

clue.text: See a spiteful person no one backed get a place

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
a cat is slang for a spiteful woman

indicators.note: backed means turned backwards, so the two pieces before it are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Watch a malicious person nobody supports find somewhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reads as supported, but it turns NO and I into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A location is a site or position, the same as a place.

clue.text: Pole fired and cold-shouldered

parts.note: S is the South Pole
lighted means set on fire

explanation.surface: A Polish man was sacked and snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish man, and 'fired' like sacked; they are S and set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To be slighted is to be snubbed or ignored, as when given the cold shoulder.

clue.text: Alarming disturbance at the border

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs things up, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Trouble breaking out on a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginal describes what lies at the edge or margin of something.

clue.text: Fruit-some cool it-chill it, even

indicators.note: some of the words that follow is taken, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: Advice to chill a piece of fruit, even to cool it down.
explanation.definitionFit: The litchi, also spelt lychee, is a sweet Chinese fruit with a rough red skin.

clue.text: Spot for Oriental secret agent

parts.note: E is short for east, the Orient
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A place set aside for an Eastern spy.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, to spot.

clue.text: Misrepresenting males, she's really outrageous

indicators.note: misrepresenting gives a false version, so the letters of the words after it are shown in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman telling lies about men is behaving disgracefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shameless has no sense of shame, and so behaves in an outrageous, brazen way.

clue.text: Guard marking time

explanation.surface: A sentry pacing up and down while waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a lookout or guard on duty, and also a wristwatch, an instrument that marks the time.

clue.text: A state service

explanation.surface: A government ceremony or official function.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass. is the short form for Massachusetts, a US state; Mass is also the Catholic church service of the Eucharist.

clue.text: Left over in a bar

indicators.note: in puts the word for finished inside the stripe

parts.note: a band is a stripe or bar of colour
done means finished, over

explanation.surface: Something left behind in a pub at closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left over' looks like one phrase, but splits: 'Left' is the definition and 'over' is DONE, which goes inside A BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned means deserted, given up and left behind.

clue.text: Further troubles met in the past

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for the past

parts.note: yore is an old word for times long past

indicators.note: troubles stirs up the word before it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: More problems faced long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubles' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal acting on 'met'; 'in' then places the result after the first letter of the old word for the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet more means in addition, a still greater amount, as further does.

clue.text: A woman with child must receive money, that's clear

indicators.note: receive means take in, so the coin goes inside

parts.note: a woman with a child is a parent
P stands for penny, money

explanation.surface: An expectant mother needs financial support, obviously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woman with child' suggests pregnancy, but means a mother: A PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means plainly visible or obvious, as clear does.

clue.text: A girl goes in to the head on her knees!

indicators.note: goes in to means enters, so the name sits inside

parts.note: the pate is the top of the head
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman bows her head and kneels.
explanation.definitionFit: The patellae are kneecaps, the bones at the front of the knees.

clue.text: Calm when bill is discovered in coat

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: plate is a thin coating of metal, as in silver plate
AC is the short form for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Keeping one's temper on finding an invoice in a jacket pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' looks like a garment but here means a thin metal layer, as in gold plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate is to pacify or soothe someone who is angry.

clue.text: Every ace perhaps has aspiration

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word may come out differently, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: aspiration is the breathy sound written H

explanation.surface: Any top tennis player has ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' reads as ambition, but in phonetics it is a breathed H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Each and every both refer to all members of a group taken one by one.

clue.text: A good man stocks an alternative variety

indicators.note: stocks means holds or keeps inside, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: a good man is a saint, abbreviated ST
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A decent shopkeeper keeps a second choice on the shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocks' reads as a shopkeeper's verb; here it means contains, the saint's abbreviation holding the alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a kind or type, the same as a variety.

clue.text: Skinhead frisked when betrayed to the police

parts.note: read as head of skin, its first letter, S
to frisk is to skip and hop about playfully

explanation.surface: A thug searched by officers was informed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frisked' suggests a police search but means jumped playfully: HOPPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopped is British slang for informed on someone to the authorities.

clue.text: Clash caused by work-stoppage

explanation.surface: A dispute brought on by industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a blow or clash, and also a walkout, a refusal to work.

clue.text: Condescends to find Europeans sound

indicators.note: sound means as heard, so the letters entered match a word said aloud

parts.note: Danes are people from Denmark

explanation.surface: Lowering oneself to discover that Scandinavians are healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' reads as healthy, but signals that DANES heard aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to doing something beneath one's dignity, to condescend.

clue.text: These days housing people better

indicators.note: housing means sheltering inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era of the calendar
people taken as men, the human race

explanation.surface: Modern times are giving homes to folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb here, to improve, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text or law is to improve or correct it.

clue.text: A note on game as savoury food

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the note follows the game

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game played with mallets and hoops
te is a note of the sol-fa scale, also written ti

explanation.surface: A message written on a sports scorecard listed with a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a small fried roll of mashed potato, meat or fish coated in breadcrumbs.

clue.text: Nut-cracker that is given free

indicators.note: a cracker breaks the word before it apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A nutcracker is handed out as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to undo knots, setting something loose.

clue.text: Genial characters built this capital suburb

indicators.note: the characters, or letters, of the word before are used to build something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Friendly people put up a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: EALING is a district in west London, famous for its film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Ealing is a borough in the suburbs of London, the British capital.

clue.text: Discerning use of dope in pain

indicators.note: in puts the drug inside the word for pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
pot is slang for cannabis, dope

explanation.surface: Taking drugs while hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use of' is a link joining the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotting means noticing or picking out, as discerning does.

clue.text: To do one's best without a tip is now in vogue

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to try is to do one's best
a tip is an end, as of a finger

explanation.surface: Making an effort without leaving a gratuity is fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but in its old sense it means outside, so the effort wraps round the tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trendy is fashionable at the present moment.

clue.text: Vain head's indolence

parts.note: vain and idle both mean pointless, as in idle threats
a ness is a head or headland, as in Dungeness on the English coast

explanation.surface: A conceited person's laziness.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is laziness, a reluctance to work.
